sections.title: Meeting someone for the first time
sections.summary: Take your time. A good match will understand.
points: Talk in the app for a while before you share your phone number or meet.
Meet in a public place during the day and tell a family member or friend where you are going.
Arrange your own transport so you can leave when you want to.
You never have to meet, share a number or send a photo. You can say no at any time.

sections.title: Requests for money
sections.summary: Nobody who is serious about marriage needs your money before you meet.
points: Never send money, airtime or mobile money to someone you haven't met, whatever the reason.
Be careful if someone asks for help with fees, travel, medical bills, a parcel or an investment.
Report anyone who asks you for money. You don't have to prove anything.

sections.title: Spotting fake profiles and scams
sections.summary: Some people are not who they say they are.
points: Be careful if a profile pushes you to leave the app quickly or to share private details.
Be careful if their story keeps changing or they avoid meeting in person.
Be careful if they say they love you very fast.
Report profiles that look fake, pretend to be someone else, or hide that they are married.

sections.title: Protecting your privacy
sections.summary: Share only what you are comfortable with, when you are ready.
points: Don't share your home address, workplace, ID numbers or bank details.
Never share a one-time code from your phone with anyone.
You can block anyone at any time. They are not told.

sections.title: Blocking and reporting
sections.summary: Both are in the app, on every profile and conversation.
points: Blocking is immediate and private. You and the other person will no longer see or contact each other.
Reporting sends the details to our safety team. You can block and report at the same time.
If your account is restricted, you can appeal the decision from the safety screen.

sections.title: If you are in danger
points: If you are in immediate danger, call the Uganda Police emergency number 999 or 112.
Move to a safe place and contact someone you trust.
Once you are safe, report the person in the app.
